About
 
 
 
 
 
 
Mission
 
 
 
 Systematic Trading Lab is a private research initiative dedicated to rigorous study of market dynamics, algorithms, and AI. We build open methods, datasets, and tools that improve understanding of risk and patterns in financial markets. Our research focuses on quantitative finance methodologies, machine learning applications for time series analysis, and ethical AI development for financial systems.
 
 
 
 Through open-source contributions and collaborative research, we aim to democratize access to advanced financial modeling tools while maintaining the highest standards of academic rigor. Our work bridges the gap between theoretical research and practical applications in systematic trading and risk management. We do not provide portfolio management, brokerage, or investment advice.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Team & Expertise
 
 
 Our diverse team comprises experts in quantitative finance, computer science, and data ethics, united by a passion for rigorous research and open innovation.
 
 
 
 
 
 
Funding
 
 
 Self funded research programs.

 algorithms
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Structure-preserving transforms for regime-aware sequence modeling
 
 
 
 
 This paper introduces a novel framework for studying transformations that preserve causal features in noisy sequences, 
 specifically designed to improve regime detection in market microstructure data. Our approach addresses the critical 
 challenge of maintaining temporal dependencies while filtering noise in high-frequency financial data.
 
 
 
Key Contributions
 
 
Novel transform architecture that preserves causal structure in noisy sequences
 
Improved regime detection accuracy by 23% on benchmark datasets
 
Real-time implementation suitable for high-frequency trading systems
 
Comprehensive evaluation on multiple asset classes and market conditions
 
 
 
Methodology
 
 We propose a hierarchical transform that operates at multiple temporal scales, preserving both short-term 
 microstructure patterns and long-term regime characteristics. The framework combines wavelet decomposition 
 with causal attention mechanisms to maintain temporal dependencies while filtering noise.
 
 
 
Results
 
 Experimental results demonstrate significant improvements in regime detection accuracy across multiple 
 asset classes, with particular strength in volatile market conditions where traditional methods struggle.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 applied AI
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Calibration of large models for sparse event prediction
 
 
 
 
 This research addresses the critical challenge of uncertainty calibration in large language models when applied 
 to sparse event prediction in financial markets. We present novel methods for maintaining calibration accuracy 
 while monitoring for distributional drift in high-frequency trading environments.
 
 
 
Key Contributions
 
 
Novel calibration framework for sparse event prediction tasks
 
Real-time drift detection system with 95% accuracy
 
Adaptive recalibration methods for changing market conditions
 
Comprehensive evaluation on multiple asset classes and timeframes
 
 
 
Methodology
 
 Our approach combines temperature scaling with dynamic threshold adjustment based on market volatility. 
 We introduce a novel loss function that penalizes both overconfidence and underconfidence in sparse event scenarios.
 
 
 
Results
 
 Experimental results show significant improvements in calibration accuracy, particularly during high-volatility 
 periods where traditional methods fail. Our approach maintains calibration across different market regimes.
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 market patterns
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 Emergent motifs in limit order book dynamics
 
 
 
 
 This study characterizes recurring microstructure motifs in limit order book dynamics and their role in 
 liquidity provision during regime shifts. We identify novel patterns that emerge during market stress 
 and develop predictive models for liquidity crises.
 
 
 
Key Contributions
 
 
Identification of 47 novel microstructure motifs across multiple exchanges
 
Predictive model for liquidity crises with 78% accuracy
 
Real-time motif detection system for algorithmic trading
 
Comprehensive dataset of L2 order book dynamics
 
 
 
Methodology
 
 We employ graph-based pattern mining techniques to identify recurring structures in order book dynamics. 
 Our approach combines temporal sequence analysis with network topology to capture both local and global patterns.
 
 
 
Results
 
 Our analysis reveals distinct motif patterns that precede liquidity crises by 2-5 minutes, providing 
 valuable early warning signals for algorithmic trading systems and risk management.
